content.overview: BNS s. 320 — Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors. BNS restatement of IPC 421. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 421. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 320 is the rule on “Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors”. The section provides that whoever dishonestly or fraudulently removes, conceals or delivers to any person, or transfers or causes to be transferred to any person, without adequate consideration, any property, intending thereby to prevent, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby prevent, the distribution of that property according to law among his creditors or the creditors of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 320 exists so that “Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 320 (Dishonest or fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent distribution among creditors), Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever dishonestly or fraudulently removes, conceals or delivers to any person, or transfers or causes to be transferred to any person, without adequate consideration, any property, intending thereby to prevent, or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby prevent, the distribution of that property according to law among his creditors or the creditors of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 320 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 320 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
